title: Ji Chang-wook and Imada Mio’s Korean-Japanese Romcom ‘Merry Berry Love’ Sets October Disney+, Hulu Bow
description:
Korean-Japanese romantic comedy series “Merry Berry Love,” starring Ji Chang-wook and Imada Mio, is bowing on Disney+ and Hulu this October.

	Set o
body:
Korean-Japanese romantic comedy series “Merry Berry Love,” starring Ji Chang-wook and Imada Mio, is bowing on Disney+ and Hulu this October.

	Set on a picturesque Japanese island, the series follows Karin Shirahama, a strawberry farmer who pours everything into her land, and Lee Yubin, a city dweller whose fortunes have taken a sharp turn for the worse. A spectacularly awkward first encounter gives way to an unlikely misunderstanding that keeps the pair far closer than either expected.
	

	Ji Chang-wook, known for “The Worst of Evil” and “The Manipulated,” plays Lee Yubin, a space planner navigating life well outside his comfort zone. Imada Mio, who appeared in “Tokyo Revengers,” takes the role of Karin Shirahama. The casting unites one of Korea’s most recognizable leading men with a prominent Japanese star, signaling the show’s deliberate cross-cultural pitch.


	Behind the camera, the series is co-directed by Kim Soojung (“Semantic Error”) and Noh Youngsub (“My Lovely Liar”), with a screenplay by Lee Jaeyoon, writer of “Divorce Insurance.” It was developed and produced by CJ ENM – the Korean entertainment company behind global hits “Crash Landing on You” and “Queen of Tears” – alongside Disney, with Nippon TV serving as co-producer.

	“Merry Berry Love” joins an expanding Asian originals slate on Disney+ and Hulu, which already carry Korean romantic titles including “Perfect Crown,” about a grand prince who enters a marriage of convenience with the heir to a Korean conglomerate, and “Soundtrack #1,” centered on a struggling songwriter and her best friend of 19 years.
	

	The series streams on Disney+ and Hulu from Oct. 7.

schema.headline: Ji Chang-wook and Imada Mio’s Korean-Japanese Romcom ‘Merry Berry Love’ Sets October Disney+, Hulu Bow

title: David Byrne Returns to Oscar Race With Original Song for Elon Musk Documentary ‘Musk’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
David Byrne wrote a song about the world’s richest man.

	The Talking Heads frontman wrote and performed an original song for “Musk,” Alex Gibney‘s
body:
David Byrne wrote a song about the world’s richest man.

	The Talking Heads frontman wrote and performed an original song for “Musk,” Alex Gibney‘s sprawling documentary reckoning with Elon Musk, Variety can exclusively reveal. Titled “Let Me Sell You a Dream,” the track plays within the 235-minute film and arrives as an Oscar-qualifying entry in the best original song race.


	Byrne wrote the song with the documentary’s composer Daniel Pemberton, the Oscar-nominated musician behind “Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse” and “The Trial of the Chicago 7.”
	

	“I was thrilled when David agreed to write (with our composer Daniel Pemberton) and perform the final song in the film,” Gibney says. “I am a huge fan of his. My wife and I were at the Pantages for the filming of ‘Stop Making Sense,’ so I sensed that he would find a musical way into what the film is trying to say. And he did. ‘Let Me Sell You a Dream’ is kick-ass. And, in writing the lyrics, David dug deep into the sayings of Musk himself to get to ‘extremely hard core,’ foot-tapping sardonic poetry.”




	

									Photo: Shervin Lainez
	



	For Byrne, the lyrics required little invention. “A thrill to collaborate with Pemberton and get invited to do this as a fan of Gibney’s films,” he says. “I asked for good quotes from the Martian, and found more of them online. I’m sure he loves dropping these wild statements, and those became the lyrics. All his own words. No editorializing. Straight from the man’s mouth to mine.”

	For Byrne, the collaboration reopens a door he last walked through nearly four decades ago. He won the Academy Award for best original score for “The Last Emperor” in 1988, sharing the honor with Ryuichi Sakamoto and Cong Su. A nomination for “Let Me Sell You a Dream” would mark his first return to the Oscar race since. Pemberton earned a best original song nod in 2021 for “Hear My Voice,” co-written with Celeste for “The Trial of the Chicago 7.”
	

	The song will be entered for best original song at the 2027 Oscars by way of the film’s theatrical run. Bleecker Street releases “Musk” in U.S. theaters on Oct. 16, a berth that clears the category’s eligibility requirements.

	Early buzz surrounding the film, described in some quarters as “scathing” and billed by Gibney himself as a “definitive and unvarnished examination” of the businessman, has been strong. “Musk” world premieres out of competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on Sept. 8 before continuing to the Toronto International Film Festival. At just shy of four hours, it stands among the most ambitious nonfiction portraits of Gibney’s career.

	Gibney first revealed in March 2023 that he had begun work on the documentary and was “many months” into production. Musk responded to news of the project on his X/Twitter account by predicting it would be “a hit-piece.” Gibney fired back on the same platform, asking “how would you know?”

	Gibney directs and produces “Musk,” joined by Jessie Deeter and Erin Edeiken for Jigsaw Productions, Dana O’Keefe for Double Agent, Joey Marra and Zhang Xin for Closer Media and Anonymous Content’s Nick Shumaker and Jessica Grimshaw. Ronan Farrow and Lawrence Wright round out the producing team.

schema.headline: David Byrne Returns to Oscar Race With Original Song for Elon Musk Documentary ‘Musk’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Andrew Garfield Renews Calls for a Gay Spider-Man, 13 Years After Asking ‘Why Can’t He Be Into Boys?’
description: Andrew Garfield is reflecting on his viral interview from 2013 in which he questioned why there had not yet been a gay Spider-Man. The Oscar nominee
body:
Andrew Garfield is reflecting on his viral interview from 2013 in which he questioned why there had not yet been a gay Spider-Man. The Oscar nominee was promoting “The Amazing Spider-Man 2” at the time when he told Entertainment Weekly about a recent discussion he had with producer Matt Tolmach about gender-swapping Peter Parker’s iconic love interest Mary-Jane, since she’s also just known as MJ.

	“I was kind of joking, but kind of not joking about MJ… I was like, ‘What if MJ is a dude?’” Garfield said in 2013. “Why can’t we discover that Peter is exploring his sexuality? It’s hardly even groundbreaking! … So why can’t he be gay? Why can’t he be into boys?”
	

	Garfield even pitched having Michael J. Bordan join his “Amazing Spider-Man” franchise as a male MJ, adding: “I’ve been obsessed with him since ‘The Wire.’ He’s so charismatic and talented. It’d be even better — we’d have interracial bisexuality!”

	Now on his 2026 press tour for Paul Greengrass’ “The Uprising,” Garfield was asked by EW to reflect on his 13-year-old call for a gay Spider-Man.

	“It was an exercise in rebellion that I felt passionate about,” Garfield said. “I just still believe that anyone can be in that suit. That’s the point of why it’s such a kind of universally beloved character, one of the greatly beloved characters in the history of fiction is because you don’t see skin color, you don’t see gender, you don’t see sexuality. Anyone can project themselves into that suit.”  

	Garfield continued, “I like the idea of a place where everyone is being honored and everyone is being included, and it was just a kind of act of saying, ‘Well, why not?’ And you’ll be telling on yourself if you have a strong opinion either way.”
	

	Tom Holland currently holds the title of Spider-Man on the big screen, with his latest outing, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” breaking box office records this summer to become one of the top grossers in film history. The actor has already expressed interest in diversifying the role with the addition of a live-action Miles Morales. Holland told the AP on the “Brand New Day” press tour that he has a “desire to bring Miles to the screen” and to “shepherd the lucky young kid who gets that job.”

schema.headline: Andrew Garfield Renews Calls for a Gay Spider-Man, 13 Years After Asking ‘Why Can’t He Be Into Boys?’

title: DreamWorks Remote Workers Ratify First Union Agreement With the Animation Guild
description:
Remote workers at DreamWorks Animation have ratified their first collective bargaining agreement.

	The agreement was ratified on Aug. 21, with 97 p
body:
Remote workers at DreamWorks Animation have ratified their first collective bargaining agreement.

	The agreement was ratified on Aug. 21, with 97 percent of participants voting in favor of the contract. Of the 108 eligible voters, 90 cast ballots, representing 83.3% of voter turnout.

	Until recently, remote animation artists and technicians working on the same projects as their Los Angeles counterparts did not receive the same wage scales, benefits or protections. 
	

	Remote workers are now on parity with on-campus workers, including pension and healthcare coverage. The newly-ratified agreement gives the unit all the same protections offered in the IATSE Local 839 Master Agreement through a Sideletter.


	Anthony Holden, DreamWorks Story Artist and member of the Negotiation Committee said, “This contract is a huge victory for DreamWorks remote artists, but also for the animation industry as a whole.” He added, “Our coworkers who work in-person at studios in L.A. enjoy mobility between employers with guaranteed benefits such as healthcare coverage and a pension plan. Many of us remote DreamWorkers have served for years (and in some cases decades) in the same industry without the same protections. Now we can work under the same terms as our union brothers and sisters. This contract represents an important shift towards broader industry change that values and respects not only artists’ skills but also our right to choose to live in locations around the country that are best for our families and personal circumstances.”

	Under the agreement, remote working animators will receive the same healthcare and pension plans as on-campus workers, with $0 premiums for individuals. 
	

	In addtion, the agreement establishes the same minimum wage standards that apply under TAG’s MasterAgreement. The lowest-paid remote artist covered by the agreement will see compensation increase from $40.82 per hour to $62.22 per hour. This represents a 52.4% wage increase.

	The unit includes remote workers across the U.S. doing work traditionally covered under TAG’s Master Agreement when performed in L.A. County, including Story Artists, Animators, Character Effects Artists, Technical Directors, Lighters, Visual Development Artists, Modelers, and Production Coordinators, among others.

	Workers at Sony Pictures Animation also voted overwhelmingly on Aug. 27 to join TAG afterseeking voluntary recognition from the company. Sony declined the request and instead required workers to proceed through an NLRB election.

	The results demonstrated strong support for union representation with 95% voter participation and 84% voting in favor of unionizing.

	“Despite Sony’s deliberate attempts to challenge our movement, when the rubber hits the road, we’re all in favor of dignity and respect in the workplace.” says Grayson Arndt, Sr. Administrative Assistant. “Now it’s time to take our seat at the table.”

	Production Coordinator Maddie Rodriguez added, “It’s exciting to follow in the footsteps of so many animation production workers before us and it’s continually heartening to know that we were never alone. So many of us have wanted this for so long. Together, we are Prod Strong!”

schema.headline: DreamWorks Remote Workers Ratify First Union Agreement With the Animation Guild

title: Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going to Deliver’
description:
Tom Cruise is confident David Ellison will deliver on his promise of 30 films a year from a combined Paramount and Warner Bros.

	“I think it’s awes
body:
Tom Cruise is confident David Ellison will deliver on his promise of 30 films a year from a combined Paramount and Warner Bros.

	“I think it’s awesome,” Cruise told “The Pat McAfee Show.” “You know, here’s the thing. They’re going to deliver 30 movies. It’s a community to me. It’s not an industry. The people in these studios are not just people in the studios. They’re my family. I know we’re going to get those 30 movies. I want us all to come together as a community to help make those 30 movies. It’s not just going to be, you know, Paramount doing it. Everyone’s going to need all the help of every artist to be able to do it.” 
	

	He continued, “We do well with those, those 30 movies are going to turn into 40 movies. To have that window and what it means — it’s not good enough that I just get to make [‘Days of Thunder 2’]. I see so many talented people that I want them to have that opportunity to make the films that they want … Like you can have these artists, all these greats, they got to cut their teeth and learn in the same way that you get to act, and you’re learning. It’s you take it and the next one and the next one. Every single one of them. The Iñárritus, the Spielbergs, the Nolans, me — all the opportunities that I’ve had, I want that for every writer, every director, every producer, every artist. And the only way you do it is we have to create an abundance. Its production begets production.”


	Ellison, in trying to rally industry support behind the Paramount-Warner Bros. megamerger, has on multiple occasions claimed the combined studios will release an unprecedented 30-plus films a year. He recently pledged to AMC Theatres and Regal Cinemas that Paramount would contractually guarantee an annual 30-movie theatrical slate with 45-day windows.
	

	Cruise is a longtime Ellison friend and ally, as Skydance Media backed the “Mission: Impossible” franchise and “Top Gun: Maverick” as a co-producer. Cruise also has a first-look production deal at Warner Bros.

	Cruise went on to highlight the success of the summer 2026 box office, shouting out hits like “Obsession,” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” He asserted that the only way the industry can produce hits like those is through an increase in production and allowing the next generation of filmmakers to get up to “game speed.” 

	“When you’re making a movie, every day is game day,” Cruise said. “If we come together as a community [we can] understand what audiences want and tell our stories that you want to tell.”

	Cruise emphasized several times throughout the interview that turning Hollywood around is a “community” effort. He added that “making movies isn’t competitive” and that “the more films we make, the better it’s going to be” for a theater business that is just now getting back on its feet.

	“I remember in the ’80s, ’90s, 2000s, you’d have five films opening on the weekend, and people [went] to the movie theaters,” Cruise recalled. “You see how audiences are enjoying that experience, but we got to make them … And we have to as a community. We’ve got to help each other to do it.”

	Cruise has long made a home at Paramount, which released all eight films in his marquee “Mission: Impossible” franchise. His other collaborations with Paramount include the “Top Gun” movies, “The Firm,” “Vanilla Sky,” “Collateral,” “War of the Worlds,” “Jack Reacher,” and “Days of Thunder,” which is getting a sequel in 2028. Cruise, never shy about the affiliation, climbed the Paramount water tower for the studio’s CinemaCon 2025 presentation featurette.

	The Paramount-Warner Bros. merger is held up by a 12-stare antitrust lawsuit filed by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. The states allege the $111 billion deal would hurt competition in the theater business and in basic cable. Ellison and the Paramount Skydance team have the U.S.’s three largest theater chains, AMC, Regal and Cinemark, backing their case. Now, they have the world’s biggest movie star on their side. The states aren’t without support, however. More than 5,600 Hollywood mainstays have now signed an open letter organized by the #BlockTheMerger coalition opposing the deal between the two legacy studios. The WGA also has filed an antitrust suit seeking to block the Paramount-WBD deal.

schema.headline: Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going to Deliver’

title: ‘VIII: Awakening’ Wraps Production in Beijing, Marking KC Global Media Asia’s First China Original (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Production has wrapped in Beijing on “VIII: Awakening,” KC Global Media Asia’s fantasy adventure drama reimagining a classic Chinese mythology legen
body:
Production has wrapped in Beijing on “VIII: Awakening,” KC Global Media Asia’s fantasy adventure drama reimagining a classic Chinese mythology legend for modern audiences. 

	The S-grade series, the company’s first original China production, completed 24 15-minute episodes for its debut season.

	The story follows insurance investigator Lu Xian, who awakens a mysterious precognitive power and discovers he is descended from an ancient legendary guardian. He must join forces with seven others to thwart a dangerous plot as an imprisoned clan of dragons threatens its return. The group uncovers betrayal within its own ranks and faces a battle for the fate of the world, ultimately awakening their true powers and restoring peace, though a new threat emerges quietly in the shadows. The series centers on Immortals whose supernatural gifts let them fight evil and protect those in need, combining suspense with fantasy and gentle humor.
	

	The cast is led by emerging actor Zhang Wan Ying (“Glory”) as He Haining, Leo Zhou (“Relying on Favors”) as Dong Fang Shuo and Nick Shan (“Creation of The Gods I: Kingdom of Storms”) as Lu Xian.


	Yu Ji, a noted director of internet midform series, directed “VIII: Awakening.” KC Global Media Asia partners Andy Kaplan and George Chien executive produced. Meng Xun, who has worked with directors including John Woo and Wong Kar-Wai, served as production designer.

	“KC Global Media Asia is looking forward to being a part of bringing such an exciting project to global audiences,” said Bonnie Wiryani, VP and head of content sales. “Viewers are more and more interested in seeing local and cultural stories developed creatively and ‘VIII: Awakening’ has all the artistry, action, mystery, fantasy and folklore that we believe will resonate widely. There is great potential for the story to grow beyond a single title and develop into a broader universe in the future.”
	

	The production is a partnership between CICC (China Intercontinental Communication Center) and Shanghai Qi’Ai Film & TV Culture Co., Ltd. This marks the first original production in China for KC Global Media Asia, which will also handle its international sales. The deal reinforces the company’s continued efforts to grow its distribution business, build creative production partnerships and deliver a broader range of high-quality stories with international appeal.

	KC Global Media Entertainment LLC is headquartered in the U.S. with offices in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, China, the Philippines and South Korea. Founded by former Sony executives Kaplan and Chien, KC Global Media Asia’s portfolio includes AXN, Animax, ONE, KCM and AXN Sports.

schema.headline: ‘VIII: Awakening’ Wraps Production in Beijing, Marking KC Global Media Asia’s First China Original (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Melissa Leo Joins Will Smith in Amazon MGM and Miramax Action-Thriller ‘Supermax’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Oscar and Emmy winner Melissa Leo has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios and Miramax’s action-thriller “Supermax,” starring Will Smith.

	David G
body:
Oscar and Emmy winner Melissa Leo has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios and Miramax’s action-thriller “Supermax,” starring Will Smith.

	David Gordon Green directs the film, which follows two FBI agents investigating a seemingly impossible murder within the impenetrable walls of a maximum-security prison. Lee — whose role remains under wraps — joins the previously announced ensemble cast led by Smith, AnnaSophia Robb, Jason Clarke, and Jaafar Jackson. The movie also features Nicholas Alexander Chavez, Andrés Almeida, Martin Bats Bradford, and Erika Ringor. 
	

	“Supermax” is currently in production in New South Wales, Australia, with Gordon Green (“Halloween”) directing from a script by David Weil and David J. Rosen (“Hunters,” “Invasion”). In May, Amazon MGM acquired the worldwide rights to the movie from Miramax for $70 million, with the film slated for release on Prime Video.


	The Picture Company’s Andrew Rona and Alex Heineman are producing the film with Smith and Adam Fishbach for Smith’s company Westbrook Studios. Weil and Rosen will also serve as executive producers alongside Miramax CEO Jonathan Glickman, president of film Alexandra Loewy, COO Thom Zadra, and senior VP Spencer Ela. James Lassiter and Miguel Melendez will also executive produce for Westbrook Studios. 

	Leo’s acclaimed filmography is highlighted by her Oscar-winning performance in David O. Russell’s “The Fighter,” plus a nomination for “Frozen River.” On TV, Leo won an Emmy for her work on FX’s “Louie.” She was previously nominated for HBO’s “Mildred Pierce” and “All The Way.” Leo’s resume also includes “King Ivory,” “The Knife,” “Prisoners,” “The Equalizer,” “Novitiate,” “I Know This Much Is True” and “I’m Dying Up Here.”
	

	Leo most recently starred in Paramount’s supernatural horror film “Passenger,” which is now streaming on Paramount+, and she just wrapped a lead role opposite Lili Reinhart in Sean Byrne’s “The Mannequin” for Studiocanal. Leo will also appear in Josh Penn Soskin’s “The Rooster Prince,” opposite Shia LaBeouf and Jackson White. She is represented by Gersh.

schema.headline: Melissa Leo Joins Will Smith in Amazon MGM and Miramax Action-Thriller ‘Supermax’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Indian Streamer JioHotstar Launches in U.K., Canada and Singapore With Interactive Features
description: India’s leading streamer JioHotstar has launched internationally in the U.K., Canada and Singapore, bringing its catalog of more than 160,000 hours
body:
India’s leading streamer JioHotstar has launched internationally in the U.K., Canada and Singapore, bringing its catalog of more than 160,000 hours of entertainment across more than 12 Asian languages alongside interactive features, personalized recommendations and new subscription options. 

	The expansion moves beyond a straightforward catalog rollout, introducing audiences in the three markets to a redesigned discovery and viewing experience built around personalization and real-time engagement, according to the company.
	

	The service was previously available in the U.K., Canada and Singapore as Hotstar. JioHotstar arrives as an all-new app, carrying the content library and product experience of JioHotstar’s India platform.


	Parent company JioStar is launching the platform with a new slate of originals, including “Ali Baba Aur Chaalis Bhoot,” “Prince of Mollywood,” “Part Timers” and “The Court,” alongside blockbuster movie premieres through the year.

	The immensely popular Indian Premier League cricket tournament and other cricket competitions JioStar owns the Indian rights for, will not be part of the launch package, Variety understands. 

	Reality franchise “Bigg Boss” returns across six languages, and for the first time, viewers in Singapore, Canada and the U.K. can cast live votes throughout each edition. Viewers in Canada and the U.K. will also get access to a 24/7 live feed, while Canada will be able to watch “Bigg Boss Hindi” seven days ahead of its television broadcast.

	Actor Anil Kapoor hosts a new game show format, “India Ka Top 1 Percent,” which will be available to audiences in Canada and Singapore.
	

	JioHotstar is also bringing content from JioStar’s television channels, including “Star Plus,” “Colors,” “Star Vijay,” “Asianet,” “Star Jalsha” and “Star Pravah.” Viewers in Singapore and Canada will get Before-TV access to popular shows including “Anupama,” “Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai,” “Seher Hone Ko Hai” and “Azhagae Azhagu,” while U.K. audiences can watch popular shows simultaneously with their television broadcast.

	The new titles join JioHotstar’s existing library, which includes originals such as “Criminal Justice,” “Special Ops,” “Chiraiya,” “Pritam & Pedro,” “Asur,” “Aarya,” “Heartbeat,” “Vikram on Duty,” “Kerala Crime Files,” “Resort” and “Kaattaan”; reality franchises including “Koffee With Karan,” “Bhojpuri Bawaal,” “Khatron Ke Khiladi,” “MTV Hustle,” “Splitsvilla,” “Laughter Chefs – Unlimited Entertainment,” “Roadies” and “Cooku With Comali”; and films including “Vaazha,” “Dhurandhar,” “Chhichhore,” “Kesari Chapter 2: The Untold Story of Jallianwala Bagh,” “Kill,” “12th Fail” and “Jab We Met.”

	JioHotstar is available on mobile and connected TV, with the app downloadable through the App Store and Google Play Store across all three markets. Android users in the U.K., Canada and Singapore can now complete sign-up entirely inside the app.

	For the first time, the company is offering a quarterly option in all three markets, giving subscribers a shorter commitment alongside its existing annual plans. Hotstar app users can download the new JioHotstar app and sign in with their existing Hotstar credentials, with their plan converting automatically to the matching JioHotstar tier. In the U.K., existing subscribers can keep their current monthly plans for as long as auto-renewal remains active.

	Updated pricing effective Sept. 2 is £19.99 ($27.20) per quarter and £69.99 ($95.20) annually in the U.K.; CAD19.99 ($14.50) per quarter and CAD49.99 ($36.30) annually in Canada; and SGD29.98 ($23.60) per quarter and SGD69.98 ($55.10) annually in Singapore.

	The platform also carries premium-quality subtitles and dubbing in more than 12 Asian languages, among them English, Hindi, Gujarati, Malayalam, Kannada and Marathi.

	“Streaming has spent the last decade competing on the size of its catalogue,” said Amit Malhotra, head – international business, JioStar. “We believe the bigger opportunity now is to reimagine how audiences experience entertainment; not just what they watch, but how they discover, engage with and shape the experience in real time. South Asian audiences have a deep connection with Indian entertainment across languages, generations and households. At the same time, audiences globally are increasingly seeking stories and cultures beyond their own. We see an opportunity to build for this broader, underserved global audience – not simply export an Indian streaming service to new markets.”
	

	“As we expand internationally, our ambition is to show what becomes possible when scale, language, cultural diversity, personalisation and deeper audience participation are built into the streaming experience from day one,” Malhotra added.

	JioStar says JioHotstar’s base of more than 500 million active users makes it one of the largest streaming platforms worldwide, pointing to features such as conversational voice discovery, AI-driven personalization and in-app commerce as part of its broader product strategy.

schema.headline: Indian Streamer JioHotstar Launches in U.K., Canada and Singapore With Interactive Features

title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Suspended, Position Will Be Recast
description:
“Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended from the game show, producer Sony Pictures Television has confirmed. 

	The decision to
body:
“Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended from the game show, producer Sony Pictures Television has confirmed. 

	The decision to remove Thornton, who has been with “Wheel of Fortune” since 2010 (and “Celebrity Wheel of Fortune” since 2021), was first reported by TMZ. The website reported that the suspension came in light of an incident on a commercial flight in May, when a passenger told a flight attendant expressed concerns about Thornton. TMZ wrote that “sources with direct knowledge tell us the pilot called ahead to have law enforcement meet Thornton when they arrived at the gate.”
	

	“We have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton,” Sony Pictures TV said in a statement. “He has been suspended from ‘Wheel of Fortune’ and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation.”  


	Thornton has been a local media presence in Los Angeles for decades, having previously worked as an afternoon anchor on KNX 1070 Newsradio, which he first joined in 1985 as a traffic reporter with Metro Traffic. He also provided traffic reports on KCBS-TV.

	His other broadcast credits include Westwood One Radio Networks, and he was the voice of L.A.’s KCOP-TV for four years. He has received an Edward R. Murrow award, Golden Mike awards and an Emmy. 

	The announcer joined “Wheel” after the death of the show’s previous announcer, Charlie O’Donnell, and has also worked as a substitute announcer on “The Price Is Right.” 

	Thornton’s other credits include “Celebrity Deathmatch,” where he voiced Johnny Gomez, and as an announcer on “The Cleveland Show” and “Tim & Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!” He’s also been heard on several video games and appeared as a commercial narrator in the 2001 animated film “Monsters, Inc.” He also voiced the 2011 Oscar-nominated short animated film “Let’s Pollute.”

schema.headline: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Suspended, Position Will Be Recast

title: Ariana Grande Tears Up as She Ends ‘Eternal Sunshine’ Tour Ahead of Step Back From Visibility: ‘I Have Loved Every Minute of This’
description: Ariana Grande took a moment during the final show of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour to thank the audience at London’s O2 Arena, sharing how it’s been a
body:
Ariana Grande took a moment during the final show of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour to thank the audience at London’s O2 Arena, sharing how it’s been an “extraordinary experience” across her 41 shows.

	“I just want to say thank you so much,” said Grande, seated on a stool on the B-stage. “This has been such an extraordinary experience. Thank you for 10 beautiful London shows and for 41 incredible Eternal Sunshine tour shows.


	“This has been one of the most beautiful, extraordinary experiences of my life and I just want to express my gratitude without sobbing completely,” she continued, choking back tears. “But really, thank you from the bottom of my heart, it’s been so special and I’ll cherish this experience always and I have the best fans in the entire world and I always have. And I love your outfits, I love your faces, I love seeing you, I love connecting with you in this way. Thank you for all of your effort for making this so special. All your messages and your costumes and your wardrobe and makeup is just so beautiful. I have loved every minute of this with you all and I just want to make sure I express how grateful I am. Thank you and I love you so much.”
	


	Grande kicked off her “Eternal Sunshine” tour in June with a trio of shows at Oakland Arena in California. Throughout the North American trek, she performed a handful of shows in various markets including Los Angeles, Austin, Atlanta, New York City, Boston, Montreal and Chicago. In mid-August, she traveled across the Pond for 10 shows at London’s O2 Arena, where she brought the journey to a close on Tuesday evening.
	

	During the tour, Grande declared that she would be stepping out of the spotlight for an extended break following its conclusion. In early August, a rep for Grande cited “ongoing public scrutiny” as one of the reasons for the pause, and said that she “looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both happily and healthily.” In tandem, Grande bowed out of Stephen Sondheim’s West End revival of “Sunday in the Park With George.”

	Grande later clarified that the break, which was announced amid speculation about her well-being and health, was planned in advance and was not a “reactive or impulsive thing.” “It is something that I had decided to plan that I had quietly made a long time ago and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the crowd in Chicago in early August. “And I want you to know many things can be true at the same time. I want to share this because I heard that my fans were worried that negativity was ruining things for me, but I just have to say that could not be more the fuck opposite. Honestly, this is not what that is.”

schema.headline: Ariana Grande Tears Up as She Ends ‘Eternal Sunshine’ Tour Ahead of Step Back From Visibility: ‘I Have Loved Every Minute of This’

            Travis Kelce has a lavish new home waiting for him in Ohio ... purchasing a massive lakefront mansion just months before his wedding to Taylor Swift ... TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            The Kansas City Chiefs tight end bought the Cleveland area estate March 2 for $5.35 million ... and we're told he was the only person who purchased the property.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            David Ayers and Nick Zawitz of The Agency Cleveland tell TMZ ... the property is set on 3.5 acres along Lake Erie, this remarkable Bratenahl estate pairs Gilded Age grandeur with modern luxury. They add they're thrilled for the new owners and so excited for Cleveland.
      
    
            The mansion features 8 bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and more than 21,000 square feet of living space.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The home recently underwent a yearlong transformation ... with nearly every detail restored or replaced, including the original door hardware, intricate walnut and oak carvings, cut glass leaded windows and multiple fireplaces.
      
    
            The third floor and lower level includes a game room and home theater in the original ballroom. The lower level boasts a billiards room, poker area, bar, temperature controlled wine cellar and tasting room, fitness center and sauna.
      
    
            Outside, a stone terrace leads to a bluestone patio and heated pool overlooking the lake.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Travis and Taylor celebrated their July 4 wedding at Madison Square Garden.
      
    
            As TMZ reported in 2023, Travis previously upgraded his Kansas City living situation with a gated mansion he bought for just under $6 million.

body:
Milo Yiannopoulos
                          I'm Already Back on Ye's Payroll ... After Deportation
                      
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Getting deported isn't stopping Milo Yiannopoulos from getting back to work ... he says he's already back on the clock working for Kanye West.
      
    
            He told Piers Morgan on Tuesday that Kanye had been "in touch" since he was apprehended by ICE in Louisiana and sent back to the UK.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            During the chat, Milo tells Piers that his boss checked in to see if was okay following his encounter with immigration officers.
      

            He says he's been back to work for 2 days ... explaining he manages Ye's lawyers, which he claims he can do "from anywhere."
      
    
            As you know, DHS revealed that Milo -- a UK citizen who legally entered the U.S. in 2019 -- had "overstay[ed] his welcome."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The agency says an immigration judge ordered Milo to be removed July 22 after he failed to show for an immigration hearing.
      
    
            Check the clip ... when Piers asked Milo if Ye believes his deportation was a "miscarriage of justice," Milo kind of deflects and pivots -- although he did tell Piers he's ashamed he supported Donald Trump.
      
    
            He just said he reassured his boss that he'd be back to work ASAP ... apologizing for the "distraction" and "irritation" his deportation caused.

                September 1, 2026
                
                            11:44 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 1, 2026
                                4:02 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Repairs are underway at Dolly Parton's star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame after a fan reported it was scratched up ... one week after the country music icon's death ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Video captured by KNX shows crews working to replace the star after Dolly's name was scratched off. The star was dedicated in her honor in 1984.
      
    
      
      Repairs are underway at Dolly Parton's star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame after it was vandalized. Video on social media showed Parton's name scratched off. No word on any suspects, but has anyone seen Jolene lately? pic.twitter.com/2WAuvb7dEJ
              @knxnews
          
  
    
            Ana Martinez, a spokesperson for the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce, tells TMZ ... Dolly's star already had cracks in it, and the chamber had scheduled it to be repaired Tuesday.
      
    
            Martinez tells us a fan reported last night that someone had stolen flowers from the star and scratched it up.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Dolly died last Tuesday at 80 following a brief battle with cancer. She was surrounded by loved ones at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville when she passed.
      
    
            Dolly's death came as a shock even to people close to her who knew she'd been dealing with health problems.
